answer: In an agent economy mapping karst aquifers, agents bid for jobs such as tracing an inlet or measuring the water table at its seasonal nadir. The market allocates bidding capacity in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than identity count. Splitting one stake across a thousand fake agents therefore buys no extra capacity. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
